Read-only investigation in /opt/nxeon. The migration engine `worker/migrate-real.ts` classifies a run as COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES when not every source domain serves on the target. I'm running an automated rehearsal loop; its results are appended to `/opt/nxeon/rehearsal-report.jsonl` (JSON lines; each has single/multi migration outcomes + logTail). You can also query the latest migrations directly: `cd /opt/nxeon && node -e "const{PrismaClient}=require('@prisma/client');const p=new PrismaClient();p.migration.findMany({orderBy:{createdAt:'desc'},take:6,select:{status:true,sourceHost:true,lastError:true,log:true}}).then(r=>console.log(JSON.stringify(r,null,1))).finally(()=>p.\$disconnect())"` (the log field holds the full human-readable migration log).

Produce a PRIORITIZED TAXONOMY of every distinct reason these migrations end COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES or FAILED, from the report + the migration logs + reading the engine code. For each distinct issue:
- One-line symptom (quote the log).
- Root cause (read the code to confirm — file:line).
- Whether it's a REAL ENGINE BUG (should be auto-fixed) or correct DETECT-AND-INSTRUCT behavior (a wrong auto-fix would be worse — e.g. stale env values, build-baked URLs, DNS-not-moved).
- For real bugs: a concrete minimal fix sketch.

Rank the real bugs by how many domains/steps they block. Ignore the already-known+fixed "source has no rsync → tar fallback" issue. Do NOT edit files; report only. Read the actual logs and code — be concrete.

# Migration failure taxonomy — `worker/migrate-real.ts`

**Timeline caveat that reframes the whole report:** `worker/migrate-real.ts` was edited at **22:09** *during* your rehearsal loop. The 5 rehearsal-report cycles (21:35–21:38) and the older DB rows are **pre-edit**; the newest COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES runs (22:16–22:26) are **post-edit**. Two of the loudest failure classes are gone in the current code — I verified against the live source, not just the logs. DB status counts: 20 FAILED, 4 COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES, 4 DONE, 1 RUNNING.

---

## A. REAL ENGINE BUGS

### A1. Source read-only guard false-positive — *blocks 100% of a run at the inventory step* — **appears already fixed at 22:09**
- **Symptom (quoted):** `ERROR: source read-only guard refused a possible WRITE command: export LC_ALL=C if command -v timeout ... FMT='name {{.Name}} image {{.Config.Imag` — this is **every** FAILED cycle 1–5 (single + both multi sources), aborting at *"Taking a read-only inventory of the old server."* Nothing migrates.
- **Root cause:** `SRC_WRITE_RE` at **`migrate-real.ts:235`**, enforced in `assertSourceReadOnly` (**:240–244**) via `putScript` (**:4397**). The regex flags a write verb anchored after a newline/`;`/`|`. The read-only inventory script (`srcInventoryScript`, **:1002–1185**) is ~120 lines of shell containing `/etc/passwd`, `mv -f`, etc.
- **Verification:** I ran the *current* `srcInventoryScript("")` and `("sudo -n")` through the *current* `SRC_WRITE_RE` via tsx → **`trips? false`** for both. So the offending pattern was widened/removed at the 22:09 edit. Post-22:09 runs sail past inventory into full completion, confirming the fix.
- **Classification:** REAL BUG (regex false-positive), **now resolved**, and in any case **rehearsal-scope only** — the guard is opt-in (`MIGRATE_SOURCE_READONLY=1`, **:226**), OFF for real customer migrations, so it never affected production.
- **Blast radius:** Maximum while active (every domain, every step) — but harness-only and fixed.

### A2. rsync `code 12` did not fall back to tar — *blocks all file copies for a run* — **appears already fixed at 22:09**
- **Symptom (quoted, CWI run `cmscbtjvr`, 21:43):** `copy failed for /var/www/html: rsync: connection unexpectedly closed (0 bytes received so far) [Receiver] rsync error: error in rsync protocol data stream (code 12) at io.c(232) [Receiver=3.4.1]` — repeated for **all 8 paths**, with no fallback line. Apps then can't start (empty dirs) → cascade.
- **Root cause / fix location:** The current fallback trigger at **`migrate-real.ts:4908`** explicitly matches `/code 1[27]|unexpectedly closed|0 bytes received/` and retries via `tarPull` (**:4379**, **:4910**). The failing run predates the 22:09 edit and shows no *"rsync couldn't run on the source — using the tar fallback"* line, so that branch wasn't catching `code 12` yet. Post-edit run `cmscczej` (22:16) shows rsync **succeeding** for all 8 paths.
- **Note on the underlying `code 12`:** its *cause* is environmental (rsync 3.4.1 failing to spawn over the `sshpass`-driven ssh, e.g. remote banner / self-to-self in the rehearsal), not something the engine should "fix" beyond falling back — which it now does.
- **Classification:** REAL BUG (missing fallback path), **now resolved**. Distinct from the known+ignored "source has *no* rsync → tar" case; this is "rsync *present* but dies mid-stream."
- **Blast radius:** All migrated files for the affected run.

### A3. Stale-reference scanner false positives — *does NOT block serving, but inflates the failed-step count* — **LIVE in current code**
Two compounding bugs, both visible in the newest run `cmscd8ffx` (22:26):
- **Symptom (quoted):** `21 file(s) still reference the old server — .../source-webconfig/nginx/sites-available/soulpilates-apex:92 (72.62.240.50); .../stale-sweep.sh:10 (72.62.240.50); .../stale-sweep.sh:10 (172.17.0.1); .../stale-sweep.sh:10 (172.18.0.1); .../stale-sweep.sh:10 (172.19.0.1); .../stale-sweep.sh:10 (172.20.0.1) and 15 more`
- **A3a — Docker bridge / RFC1918 gateways used as needles.** Root cause: `ipNeedles` at **`migrate-real.ts:6220–6222`** takes `inv.srcIps` (from `hostname -I` on the source) and filters out only `targetIp` and `127.*`. On a Docker host `hostname -I` also returns `172.17.0.1` (docker0) and per-network gateways `172.18–20.0.1`. These are **identical on the new box** and are not the old server. They enter the needle set and even risk being auto-`sed`'d in allowlisted configs (rewrite pass **:6255–6275**).
  - **Fix sketch:** in the `ipNeedles` filter, also drop private/link-local ranges: `!/^(10\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\.|192\.168\.|169\.254\.)/.test(i)`. The old server's stable identity is its **public** IP only.
- **A3b — engine scans its own scratch dir.** Root cause: `scanRoots` includes migrated `paths` (**:6232**); when `/root` is migrated, `/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/` is under it. `SWEEP_EXCLUDE_DIRS` (**:3614–3618**) prunes `node_modules`, `.git`, … but **not** `nxeon-migrations`, so the sweep matches its own generated `stale-sweep.sh` (whose line 10 literally lists the needle IPs — self-match) and the deliberately-kept `source-webconfig` reference copy (**:5637–5647**). A3a feeds A3b exactly: the bridge IPs written into `stale-sweep.sh` are re-found there.
  - **Fix sketch:** add `"nxeon-migrations"` to `SWEEP_EXCLUDE_DIRS` (basename `-name` prune at **:3659** will then exclude the whole work tree), or prune `$work` explicitly in `staleSweepScript` (**:3658**).
- **Classification:** REAL BUG (detect false-positives). Report-quality only — it does not stop any domain serving, but it pads the *"N step(s) failed"* line that is part of the COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES surface.
- **Blast radius:** 0 domains, but 1 spurious failed-step per run + misleading/non-actionable file list.

## B. CORRECT DETECT-AND-INSTRUCT (auto-"fixing" would be worse) — this is what actually drives COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES

The outcome gate flips to COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES whenever `unservedDomains` is non-empty (**:182–183**, computed **:2710**, scored against the source's *own* live vhost set). In the post-fix runs the domains are dark for reasons the engine **correctly refuses to paper over**:

1. **Apps not auto-started → upstream down → 502 → domain not serving.** Quoted (`cmscd8ffx`): `docker ps shows 0 running container(s)` … `Port(s) 8391, 8491, 8392 still not up after 180s` … `serving: nexis...; NOT serving: 5 others`. The engine *does* start what it safely can (run `cms3oxbma` reached `docker ps shows 15 running container(s)`), but refuses when:
   - required compose vars would resolve empty — **:5357–5366** (*"Starting it anyway would bring up a stack with empty passwords/URLs"*),
   - a bind-mount source dir didn't arrive — **:5469–5474** (would start against an empty dir and silently lose data),
   - a container overrides cmd/entrypoint unreproducibly — blocker at **:1781**.
   Auto-forcing any of these is worse (broken stack / data loss).
2. **Files still reference the old server = build-baked frontend URLs + app data.** Report-only path **:6299–6308** (*"application files, not configuration we own … if the file belongs to a JavaScript frontend, rebuild its image afterwards"*). Correct — the right value is the customer's new domain, unknowable, and editing app data would corrupt it.
3. **Missing TLS cert for a domain whose DNS isn't here yet** (`dealerleads.me`). Quoted: *"no certificate for dealerleads.me exists here … Once dealerleads.me points at this server run: certbot …"*. Correct — DNS-not-moved; cert cannot be issued.
4. **HTTPS pending until DNS moves** (`www.soulpilates.com.vn`). Quoted: *"this name does not point at the new server yet … a certificate cannot be issued until DNS moves."* Correct — DNS-not-moved.
5. **"Sites we could not publish automatically"** — old vhost points at an app port/folder not present yet — **:5764–5782**. Correct — the app must start first; guessing a vhost would 502.

## C. TRANSIENT / ENVIRONMENTAL (not engine bugs)

- **`connect ECONNREFUSED 51.79.226.200:22`** (cycle 5, one multi source). Target SSH momentarily unavailable — retry-class, no code change warranted.

| Rank | Bug | Domains/steps blocked | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A1** read-only guard false-positive | Entire run (every domain + step), at inventory | Fixed at 22:09; rehearsal-only anyway |
| 2 | **A2** rsync code-12 no tar fallback | All files → apps → all domains for that run | Fixed at 22:09 (fallback now catches code 12) |
| 3 | **A3a/A3b** stale-scanner false positives (bridge IPs + self-scan of scratch dir) | 0 domains; 1 spurious failed-step + misleading file list per run | **Live — still present in current code** |

**Bottom line:** After the 22:09 edit, the two run-killers (A1, A2) are gone. The *persistent* COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES signal is almost entirely category **B — correct, honest detect-and-instruct** (apps needing secrets/mounts/rebuilds the engine can't safely supply, plus DNS/TLS only the customer can move). The **one real bug still worth fixing** is **A3** (`migrate-real.ts:6220-6222` and `:3614-3618`): filter RFC1918/Docker-bridge IPs out of the needle set and exclude the `nxeon-migrations` scratch dir from the sweep.
